questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: A timeline shows: 1788, the First Fleet arrives at Sydney Cove. 1851, gold is found in Victoria. 1901, the colonies join to form Australia. How many years after the First Fleet arrived was gold found in Victoria?
questions.explanation: Take the earlier year from the later year. 1851 − 1788 = 63.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: On a map, north is at the top. Mia's school is west of the park. The library is south of the park. In which direction would Mia travel from the library to the school?
questions.explanation: The school is west of the park, and the park is north of the library. So from the library, the school is north and west.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: A school recorded the rain each day. Monday: 0 mm. Tuesday: 5 mm. Wednesday: 12 mm. Thursday: 3 mm. Which day was the wettest?
questions.explanation: Wednesday had the most rain, 12 mm. That is more than any other day.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Sam wants to show the order of important events in his town's history. Which format would suit this best?
choices: A pie chart of favourite foods
questions.explanation: A timeline puts events in order by date. A map shows places, not the order of events.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: A council wants to build a new road through bushland. A shop owner says it will bring more customers. A bird watcher says it will harm the birds' homes. Why do they have different views?
choices: One of them has the wrong facts
They have not read the news
questions.explanation: The shop owner cares about business. The bird watcher cares about nature. People can see the same plan in different ways.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: A ship's officer and an Aboriginal Elder each described the arrival of the First Fleet. Their stories were very different. What is the best reason?
choices: One of them was not there
Each person saw it from their own point of view
Only the officer could tell stories
questions.explanation: People have different experiences and different things matter to them. So their accounts of the same event can differ.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Which of these is a primary source about life in Sydney in 1850?
choices: A diary written in 1850 by a Sydney resident
questions.explanation: A primary source comes from the time being studied. The diary was written in 1850 by someone who was there.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: A council asked 30 children about a new park. 22 want more shade. 5 want a bigger oval. 3 want more bins. Which conclusion fits the information?
choices: Most children want a bigger oval
Children do not want a new park
questions.explanation: 22 out of 30 children chose shade. That is more than all the other choices put together.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: A town dam was lower each month from December to March. Very little rain fell in those months. Which conclusion is best supported by these facts?
choices: The dam will be full next month
Low rainfall is a likely reason the dam level dropped
questions.explanation: The facts say little rain fell while the level dropped. The other choices are not shown by the facts.
